content: {"rule":"K-C","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge resolves a link collision by saying Acts 2:30 does not name whose body is the channel, which is the sort of verse-level silence rule K-C addresses.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"the text names the seed of David 'according to the flesh' without naming whose body is the channel, so the point stays open.","rule_words":"When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.","room":"The phrase 'never verse by verse' could be read as allowing underdetermination whenever one cited verse is silent on a detail, or as requiring the whole chains to be weighed by footing; I weigh it as the latter because K-C retires the stating-verse test.","why":"The judge kept the point open because Acts 2:30 itself does not name the channel, instead of weighing the defender's and challenger's chains by footing as K-C requires."}
